text.p: Borg-Warner Security Corp said Monday it has completed new financing arrangements totaling about $410 million.

Proceeds from financing were used to repay a bank term loan of $115 million and an existing bank revolving facility under which about $82 million was outstanding. In addition, an existing letter of credit facility is being replaced.

The financings include the issuance of $125 million face amount of 9.625 percent senior subordinated notes maturing in 2007 and a new $285 million revolving bank credit facility maturing in 2002. The bank facility provides for up to $155 million in direct borrowing and up to $155 million for letters of credit.
"This financing strengthens our capital structure, one of our top goals," said Joe Adorjan, Borg-Warner Security's chairman and chief executive officer.
"It provides significant longer term debt capacity, with improved flexibility and reduced cost for Borg-Warner Security," he said in a statement.
Borg-Warner Security provides security services including electronic and physical security services under the Wells Fargo and Burns brand names.
